title: Nebius acquires inference optimization startup Inferize to accelerate AI deployments
key_facts: Nebius, described as a 'neocloud', acquired Inferize, an inference optimization company.
Nebius claims the technology can shorten the time to launch large-scale AI models.
Inferize was founded earlier this year by alumni of Granulate and will join Nebius' Token Factory managed inference platform.
Inferize co-founders Lior Gorbonos and Guy Bortnikov previously founded Granulate, an Israel-based software optimization firm sold to Intel in 2022.
Inferize's technology cuts 'cold starts', the time models need to load before serving a request, which improves use of capacity.
Earlier this year Nebius bought Eigen AI, another optimization firm, which added autoscaling endpoints and fine-tuning pipelines.
quote_evidence: Neocloud darling Nebius acquired an inference optimization company whose technology it claims can shorten the time to launch large-scale AI models.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Among Inferize's innovations are means to cut cold starts – the time models need to load before serving a single request, thereby improving capacity utilization.
why_it_matters_hint: Nebius adds technology meant to get extra AI computing capacity ready faster when customer demand changes.
notes: Read in full. Statements come from Nebius' chief technology officer Danila Shtan and Inferize co-founder Guy Bortnikov in the company's statement; speed gains are the companies' own claims.
